Eskom Holdings Appoints New Chief Financial Officer Amid Drive for Operational Stability

Eskom Holdings SOC Ltd, South Africa’s state-owned electricity utility, announced the appointment of Naledi Mofokeng as Chief Financial Officer on Thursday, marking a significant step in the company’s ongoing efforts to strengthen its leadership team and reinforce fiscal discipline.

Mofokeng, who previously served as finance director at the Johannesburg-based infrastructure group Imvula Power, will assume her new role effective 1 July 2024. She succeeds Sipho Dlamini, who has held the position in an acting capacity since early last year.

“We are pleased to welcome Ms. Mofokeng to Eskom during a period of renewed focus on financial sustainability and operational efficiency,” said Dan Marokane, Eskom’s Group Chief Executive, in a statement. “Her extensive experience in utility finance and risk management will be invaluable as we continue to implement our turnaround strategy.”

Industry analysts have broadly welcomed the move. “Mofokeng’s track record in corporate restructuring and cost controls is well known in the sector,” said Lerato Khumalo, an energy analyst at Joburg Capital Advisors. “Eskom’s financial challenges require strong leadership, and this appointment sends a signal of commitment to prudent management.”

Eskom Holdings SOC Ltd, which generates approximately 90% of South Africa’s electricity, has faced mounting pressure to address its debt levels and improve revenue collection, though recent quarters have seen operational stability and progress in financial reporting.

The appointment comes after consultations with the Department of Public Enterprises and Eskom’s board. In a statement, the National Union of Mineworkers said, “We look forward to working with Ms. Mofokeng and hope this will contribute to greater transparency and accountability.”

Mofokeng is a qualified chartered accountant with over 18 years of experience in the energy and infrastructure sectors.
